To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cx30 channels specifically regulate the expression of γ-SG, a component of the DAPC, in astrocyte end-feet.
Cx30 channels expressed in astrocyte end-feet regulate the expression of γ-Sarcogglycan in the cerebrovacular system.
the expression of γ-Sarcogglycan is regulated by astroglia Cx30 channel expression in the cerebrovasculature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Cx43 and Cx 30 in astrocyte function.
the role of the Sarcoglycane complex in the cerebrovasculature, and its regulation by Cx30 channels.
the role of astrocytes in the cerebrovasculature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cx30 channels regulate γ-SG in the cerebrovasculature.
Cx30 channels may contribute to the regulation of Sgcg expression in the cerebrovasculature.
the SGC is expressed at the gliovasculature and is specifically regulated in the cerebrovasculature by the Cx30 channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cx30 channel activity is required for the proper regulation of γ-SG expression, which in turn may contribute to the stabilization of cerebrovascular membranes.
astroglial Cxs are involved in the regulation of the cerebrovascular SGC expression, which may contribute to the maintenance of BBB homeostasis.
Cx30 channels, in addition to their well-established role in intercellular trafficking, are also involved in the regulation of the SGC expression at the gliovasculature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cx30 channel activity is not required for BBB integrity, but it is necessary for the regulation of γ-SG expression.
Cx30 channels may regulate the expression of the γ-subunit of the SGC in the cerebrovasculature, and that the SGC may be involved in the regulation of the cerebrovascular function.
astroglia, and particularly perivascular astrocytes, may be a major regulator of the cerebrovascular physiology, through Cx30 channels.
